findings.evidence: "Remove unsupported abstractions and repetition" activates familiar editing practice, and preservation instructions recur throughout the revision sequence and safeguards. The more distinctive contributions are the exceptions involving normative force, unknown actors, control-flow conditions, and unsupported specificity.
findings.fix: Consolidate ordinary preserve-meaning and remove-repetition reminders into one short checkpoint. Keep the technical semantic exceptions prominent and demonstrate the decisions with a few difficult before/after cases rather than repeating the general policy.

findings.evidence: "When context is constrained, use an available subagent only if one exists" restates harness capability discovery and dispatch rather than supplying writing expertise or correcting a demonstrated non-obvious dispatch mistake.
findings.fix: Remove the generic delegation instruction. Retain only the writing-specific fallback: preserve a compact invariant list and consult the relevant reference section.

findings.evidence: "Mark semantic invariants before editing" begins a coherent copyediting procedure, but the description also promises original drafting. There is no comparable procedure for selecting a draft's audience, reader action, supported facts, or information order when no source prose exists.
findings.fix: Add a short original-draft branch: identify the reader and intended action, establish supported facts and required terminology, organize information around that action, draft, then apply the existing semantic and concision checks.

findings.evidence: "Make the rewrite shorter than the original" and "a one-line check quoting the original and both word counts" impose a rigid output ritual on varied prose tasks. Already-minimal text may have no shorter meaning-preserving rewrite, and quoting an entire long original defeats a concise response.
findings.fix: Check meaning and length internally by default and return only the requested prose. Permit unchanged or longer wording when fidelity or clarity requires it, explain that exception briefly, and show counts or comparison excerpts only when requested or materially useful.

findings.evidence: "Explain likely causes and how to profile it; do not copyedit my wording" occupies one of only three output cases while being outside the skill's stated scope. The remaining cases do not test the central negation, modal-force, quotation, unknown-actor, or already-concise boundaries.
findings.fix: Keep technical diagnosis as a trigger negative and add in-scope output cases covering must/should/may, an unless condition, embedded quotations or identifiers, an unknown actor, and already-minimal text. Assert preservation of each semantic invariant rather than requiring particular wording.
